ca-45-1-c-297.title: C-297 would make certain personalized prices reviewable
ca-45-1-c-297.delta: The official first-reading text resolves the earlier clause-access gap. The proposal turns on a profit purpose, a material price difference and inadequate disclosure.
ca-45-1-c-297.next: Compare each subsequent bill version with clauses 1–7 and check for committee amendments, assent and commencement.
unknowns: Application of materiality and fair disclosure to a particular Montréal transaction would depend on the facts and any enacted wording.

facts.statement: Clause 2 would add section 74.051 to the Competition Act. It covers consumers charged materially different prices for comparable goods or services for profit maximization without fair and adequate disclosure. Paragraphs (2)–(3) cover personal data and exclude adjustments based solely on generally applicable market factors.

Clause 1 would let the Competition Commissioner assist qualifying foreign investigations into this category. Existing section 74.012 requires written purpose and confidentiality commitments before disclosure, excludes foreign contraventions with penal consequences under Canadian law, and requires consideration of reciprocal assistance.

Clause 3 adds the conduct to the subsequent-order provision. Clauses 4–7 add it to electronic-commerce enforcement, disclosure and use provisions, including information flows involving the CRTC, Competition Commissioner and Privacy Commissioner. Existing section 60 requires a written agreement or arrangement and limits use and redisclosure.

ca-opc-personalized-pricing.delta: The commissioner told ETHI that consultation would open in the coming weeks and guidance was targeted for the following months. The statement leaves the opening and publication dates unspecified.
ca-opc-personalized-pricing.next: Acquire the opening notice, submission deadline and final guidance as separate events.

facts.statement: The OPC described PIPEDA expectations around appropriate purposes, meaningful consent and accessible notice. It identified browsing, purchases, location and financial inferences as examples relevant to pricing. It separately announced plans to seek input and issue guidance.
